comment: Epoch 64 of 1.3.0 (pending), EU5 1.4.7/build26377361; frozen epoch63 preserved in golden_world_epoch63.json. Wastelands are planned terrain, not the highest cells: dunes, plateaus, flat wilds under any vegetation, hills and mountains, chosen from the climate and vegetation just drawn, at the sea as inland, and sized from the vanilla impassable locations (rnw.barrens), and named for their terrain (a Highlands, a Wilds, a Desert). They are decided before the coasts, so the ports, docks and strait crossings are made for the land they leave passable. The active coasts raise cordilleras; the rivers are drawn before the land cells, which take the larger rivers as borders and are seeded as far apart as the game's locations of the class the climate vote will choose and of the ground their relief makes; the rain is that of a summer and a winter (belts moved by the season, the monsoon from the seas on the equator side, cold and warm currents) and the vote reads both; it learns from the Americas too, without farmland, its pairs weighed so that it reads vanilla's own locations as they are; the ground of every cell is voted by the vanilla locations nearest in the ranks of its height, ruggedness, roughness, rain and distance to the sea, and the wasteland plan reads that vote for the kind a cell may be. The location templates, the hierarchy, the localization in all eleven languages and the files that draw them change; the count stays 884.
